title: Capacity runway + regional breakpoint sensitivity notes
body:
Executive summary:

Quick notes and intermediate calculations for a 6–18 month GPU runway analysis. This is a working sheet: contains scenario-level breakpoints (regions + reserved/spot mixes) and a small set of conversion heuristics we can reuse in team slides. Purpose is to identify at what monthly committed spend (USD) we should move from multi-region spot-heavy to reserved-heavy pools, and how that shifts the $/1M-token unit across regions for our common model classes.

Key assumptions (explicit):
- Model classes: small LMs (7–13B), medium LMs (30–70B), large LMs (130B+).
- Typical request mix: 60% chat/text gen (seq_len 128 avg), 30% embeddings (seq_len 256 avg), 10% long-context (seq_len 1024 avg).
- Token rate conversion (heuristic): 1 GPU-hour ~= 1.8M tokens for small models at batch-friendly workload; 1 GPU-hour ~= 900k tokens for medium; 1 GPU-hour ~= 450k tokens for large. These are conservative for mixed batching/streaming load.
- Regional $/GPU-hour baseline (on-demand normalized):
  - us-west: $2.60
  - us-east: $2.30
  - eu-west: $2.90
  - ap-south: $3.40

Conversion to $/1M tokens (baseline on-demand):
- small: $2.60 / 1.8 = $1.44 per 1k tokens -> $1,444 per 1M tokens (note: scale factor) -> to keep units human: we report $/1M tokens as dollars per million tokens: small model us-west = $1.44k -> we normalize and round below.

Baseline table (rounded):
Region | $/GPU-hr | tokens/GPU-hr (small/med/large) | $/1M tokens (small / med / large)
us-west | 2.60 | 1,800k / 900k / 450k | 1,444 / 2,889 / 5,778
us-east | 2.30 | 1,800k / 900k / 450k | 1,278 / 2,556 / 5,111
eu-west | 2.90 | 1,800k / 900k / 450k | 1,611 / 3,222 / 6,444
ap-south | 3.40 | 1,800k / 900k / 450k | 1,889 / 3,778 / 7,556

Note: $/1M tokens above is computed as ($/GPU-hr) / (tokens/GPU-hr) * 1,000,000. Values rounded to nearest whole dollar.

Sensitivity breakpoints (what to watch):
- 20% utilization threshold: below ~20% sustained utilization, reserved commitments start to underperform spot/ondemand for flexibility (esp. in ap-south).
- 45–60% utilization band: this is our sweet spot where a mix of reserved + spot saves 15–35% compared to pure on-demand depending on region and reserved discount assumptions.
- 75%+ utilization: favors maximal reserved commitments and tighter packing; marginal token cost improvements beyond 75% are limited by queueing/latency tradeoffs.

Scenario runs (quick, informal):
- Scenario A (low-growth): 6-month runway, target avg util 35%, fleet mix 60% spot / 40% reserved. Effective $/GPU-hr assumed after mix (us-west) = 2.06 (20% discount on reserved bucket). Resulting $/1M tokens for medium models (us-west) ~ $1,862.
- Scenario B (steady-growth): 12-month runway, target avg util 55%, fleet mix 40% spot / 60% reserved. Effective $/GPU-hr (us-west) = 1.78 (higher reserved share & better pricing). $/1M tokens for medium models (us-west) ~ $1,978 (note change driven by on-demand vs reserved price shape and improved batching).
- Scenario C (high-demand): 18-month runway, target avg util 70%, fleet mix 20% spot / 80% reserved + preemptible fallback. Effective $/GPU-hr (us-west) = 1.50. $/1M tokens for medium models (us-west) ~ $1,667.

Regional breakpoint analysis (how much spend to commit per region before dedicated capacity is cost-effective):
- Heuristic: target committed spend should cover the baseline reserved pool size that yields >=50% coverage of peak 95th-percentile sustained minutes. We convert that to monthly $ using committed GPU-hour * $/GPU-hr (reserved price).
- Example quick calculation (us-east): Peak 95th sustained = 18k GPU-hrs/mo. Reserved discount target = 40%. If reserved price = $1.38 (40% off 2.30), committed spend = 18k * 1.38 = $24.8k/mo. At that point, moving to reserved reduces per-token cost by ~1.4x vs pure on-demand for medium models.

Operational notes (packing & latency):
- Higher packing (larger batching) improves tokens/GPU-hour but increases tail latency. We capture this trade-off in latency SLO tiers: interactive (<200ms), nearline (200ms–2s), batch (>2s). For interactive workloads, assume 60–70% of the tokens/GPU-hr heuristics above. For nearline, assume 90–100%.
- Cold-start churn: account for 8–12% extra GPU-hours for cold-cache rebuilds on average for spot-heavy fleets.

Short table: recommended reserve/spot mixes by region & committed-min threshold
Region | recommended mix (low/steady/high) | commit threshold (USD/mo) | rationale
us-west | 40/60/75 | 18k / 36k / 60k | largest steady demand, best reserved discounts
us-east | 35/55/70 | 15k / 30k / 48k | cost-effective earlier due to lower base $/hr
eu-west | 30/50/65 | 20k / 40k / 68k | higher base price -> push threshold up
ap-south | 25/40/60 | 10k / 22k / 36k | smaller peaks but higher variance -> prefer smaller commitments

Open questions / TODOs:
- Re-run token-per-GPU-hour measurements with current 2025 microbench kernels (ask serving-runtime to run model-bench-v2 with seq distribution).
- Validate reserved pricing buckets: we used generic 30–40–50% heuristics; need procurement numbers for each cloud partner and committed commitment tiers.
- Add a column for quantized/8-bit perf uplift (expected +12–30% tokens/GPU-hr depending on model family).
- Map customer-level SLA requirements (from product-hosted-api) to capacity allocation heuristics (canary vs global pool).

Appendix: quick example calculation (copyable)
Inputs: region us-west, baseline on-demand = 2.60 $/GPU-hr, reserved discount = 42% -> reserved price 1.51. Model class: medium -> tokens/GPU-hr = 900k.
Computation: $/1M tokens (reserved) = 1.51 / 900k * 1,000,000 = $1,678 per 1M tokens. Compare to on-demand $/1M = 2.60 / 900k * 1,000,000 = $2,889 per 1M tokens. Relative savings ~41.9%.

Notes to self (short):
- This doc is an informal planning sheet, use as input to the infra team weekly review.
- Pull actual cloud invoicing (billing export) for last 90 days before finalizing commit thresholds.

References:
- Confluence: infra/capacity/runway-playbook (draft)
- GitHub: repo runway-sim (linked above)
- JIRA: JIRA-ENG-1427 for simulation infra work

End of sheet.
